nfl.oneThing: The Jaguars made three trades on Monday, sending a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to Philadelphia for defensive tackle Jordan Davis. The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday.

headlines.title: Jaguars go all in before the deadline
headlines.summary: Jacksonville traded a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for Davis. The same day, the Jaguars sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Falcons for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, and sent defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Saints for a 2028 sixth-round pick. Eagles reports suggest the Davis deal may also tie into a defensive coordinator change, with Jim Schwartz mentioned as a possible replacement if Vic Fangio retires.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Jaguars are 6-2 and third in the AFC, and ESPN is asking whether they are now fully committed to a Super Bowl push. The Eagles are 2-7 and last in the NFC East, so the picks are a long-term gain for them.

headlines.title: Colts open to trading Jonathan Taylor
headlines.summary: The Colts are open to trading running back Jonathan Taylor, and several teams are reportedly interested. The Vikings, Broncos and Packers are named as possible landing spots as the deadline approaches. Indianapolis is in a rough spot and has lost five straight games.
headlines.whyItMatters: At 2-7 and 13th in the AFC, the Colts are sellers. A move would signal a rebuild, and it would give a contender a proven back for the second half.

headlines.title: Cardinals lose Gardner Minshew and Michael Wilson
headlines.summary: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew probably needs season-ending surgery on his right UCL, according to ESPN sources. Top receiver Michael Wilson is also out for the season with a neck fracture. Arizona has signed veteran quarterback Josh Johnson off the Bengals practice squad.
headlines.whyItMatters: Arizona is 3-6 and 14th in the NFC, so the losses make a tough season harder. Johnson's signing points to a quick change at quarterback rather than a long wait.

headlines.title: Patriots' Stevenson hurt in blowout loss
headlines.summary: Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson has a knee tendon issue that is not expected to need surgery. He was hurt late in the third quarter of the loss to the Packers, when New England trailed 42–14. Stevenson has played 65% of the offensive snaps, with 399 yards on 102 carries and two touchdowns. The Patriots' next game is against the Lions in Munich, and they have a bye after it.
headlines.whyItMatters: New England is 5-4 and seventh in the AFC. Its depth behind Stevenson is thin, with the third and fourth options now expected to carry the load.

teamNews.title: Raiders listening ahead of the deadline
teamNews.text: Kubiak says the Raiders are 'talking all the time' with the deadline a day away, but he gave no hint of whether they will buy or sell. A Review-Journal stock report looks at which players could be available, and a trade pitch has the Raiders landing a Cowboys all-pro for a second-round pick. That is a proposal only.

teamNews.title: Seahawks start Drew Lock again
teamNews.text: Seattle will start Drew Lock against the Raiders in Las Vegas on Sunday, 15 November, after he took the Seahawks to a 17–3 win over Arizona. Lock has an oblique injury that the Seahawks expect to manage. Sam Darnold will miss the game, and the team says he might return after its Week 11 bye.

headlines.title: Warriors' Will Richard out indefinitely
headlines.summary: The Warriors say guard Will Richard is out indefinitely with a torn UCL in his left thumb. Richard had been giving the team key minutes as both a starter and a reserve. Golden State has won seven straight games since an 0–3 start, and Richard's role has been part of that run.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Warriors are 7-3 and sixth in the West. Losing a guard who has been playing starter's minutes puts pressure on the rotation during a winning stretch.

headlines.title: Grizzlies still perfect on the road
headlines.summary: Memphis beat the short-handed Raptors 118–102 in Toronto, improving to 5-0 on the road. Ty Jerome scored 27 points and Cameron Boozer added 22 points, eight rebounds and eight assists. The Grizzlies are the only NBA team without a road loss this season. Toronto was missing Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley.
headlines.whyItMatters: Memphis is 7-3 and fifth in the West, and a perfect road record this early says a lot about its depth. Toronto is 5-5 and sixth in the East.

headlines.title: Hornets end losing streak with a rout of the Cavs
headlines.summary: Charlotte beat Cleveland 124–112 to snap a six-game losing streak. Grayson Allen scored 27 points and Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds. The Cavaliers trailed by as many as 33 points against the league's worst offence. Cleveland is 5-6 and seventh in the East, and it plays at the Knicks on national TV on Wednesday.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Cavs needed a bounce-back and did not get one. The Hornets are 4-7, and a game like this gives them a good reason to believe their bench can carry them.

headlines.title: Doc Rivers apologises to Giannis
headlines.summary: Doc Rivers says he reached out to Giannis Antetokounmpo to apologise for questioning his basketball IQ. Rivers says he meant that the force Antetokounmpo plays with can get in the way of his feel.
headlines.whyItMatters: Antetokounmpo is off to a strong start for the Heat, averaging 27.5 points and 12.8 rebounds a game. The Heat are 4-6, so the back-and-forth is one more thing to manage.

contextCard.title: How two-way contracts work
contextCard.body: A two-way contract lets a player split time between an NBA roster and the team's G League affiliate. The player can join the NBA team for a limited number of days each season, so the team can add depth without taking a full roster spot. The Grizzlies signed guard Richie Saunders to one of these deals this week.
